beginner.label: Beginner
beginner.description: The melody over a simple left hand: one bass note on beat 1 and one chord held for beats 2 and 3, with no chord of more than three notes.

original.label: Original
original.description: The piece as printed: the melody in the right hand and the left hand's held bass and chords on the grand staff, with the repeat and both endings written out.

analysis.title: Gmaj7
analysis.text: The piece opens with the left hand alone: a low G in the bass, then the chord B, D and F sharp above it. Together they make G major seventh, a G chord with the F sharp on top. It is a soft color with no pull toward another chord.

analysis.title: Small moves
analysis.text: Between bars 1 and 2 only two notes of the upper chord move: B falls to A and D falls to C sharp, while F sharp stays. The bass makes the big leap, G down to D. The ear hears one chord breathing, not two chords changing.

analysis.title: Dmaj7
analysis.text: The second bar is D major seventh: a low D with the chord A, C sharp and F sharp. D is the home chord of the piece. The two chords now alternate, bar after bar, and the home chord is never allowed to sound final.

analysis.title: Melody enters
analysis.text: The right hand enters softly, marked pp in the source, on F sharp 5. The first phrase is nine notes, F#5 A5 G5 F#5 C#5 B4 C#5 D5 A4, and it floats over the same two chords as the intro.

analysis.title: Swells
analysis.text: A hairpin grows from the F#5 of bar 5 to the C#5 of bar 7, and another fades from the D5 across the long A4 of bar 8. The left hand stays level underneath. Dynamics are read from the source file; the MIDI file ignores them.

analysis.title: Held F sharp
analysis.text: The melody holds one note, F sharp 4, for four bars (bars 9 to 12). Over Gmaj7 it is the major seventh of the chord; over Dmaj7 it is the third. The note never moves, yet its meaning changes with every bar.

analysis.title: Melody again
analysis.text: Bars 13 to 16 play bars 5 to 8 again, note for note: the same nine notes over the same two chords.

analysis.title: F sharp minor
analysis.text: The bass drops to F sharp 2 and the chord is F sharp, A and C sharp: F sharp minor, the first chord that is not Gmaj7 or Dmaj7. The melody settles on C#5.

analysis.title: B minor
analysis.text: B minor over a low B: the bass falls a fifth from F sharp. The melody climbs a fourth, from C#5 to F#5.

analysis.title: E minor
analysis.text: E minor: E2 in the bass with B and G above it. The melody drops to a long E4 held for three bars (bars 19 to 21).

analysis.title: E minor 7
analysis.text: G4, D4 and B3 over the same E bass: E, G, B and D. The bass stays and the chord gains its seventh, D, so the harmony shifts without the bass moving.

analysis.title: D minor
analysis.text: The bass is back on D2 and the chord is D, F and A. The F is natural: every F so far in the piece has been F sharp. This is the first note outside the key signature, and the color turns darker.

analysis.title: A minor
analysis.text: A minor over a low A, with a natural C in the chord. The melody starts a new rising line, A, B, C, then E, D, B, then D, C, B (bars 22 to 24), a new line with no F sharp in it.

analysis.title: D pedal
analysis.text: From bar 23 to bar 31 the bass stays on D2 and only the chord above it changes: E minor 7, A minor, D7, D minor 7. The D keeps the tonic underneath every one of them.

analysis.title: D7
analysis.text: D, F sharp, A and C: a D dominant seventh on the tonic. The F is sharp and the C is natural.

analysis.title: D minor 7
analysis.text: Over the same D bass the chord is F, C and A, with D below: D minor seventh. In the bar before, the F was sharp; now it is natural. Major turns to minor in one step.

analysis.title: Rising scale
analysis.text: E, F, G, A: the melody climbs four notes (bars 27 and 28) to A5, the highest note of the piece, then drops to C5 and D5.

analysis.title: First ending
analysis.text: Bars 32 to 39 are the first ending. The bass walks E, F sharp, B, E and the chords follow: E minor, F sharp minor, B minor, A over E. In bar 39 the music lands on D major and then goes back to bar 1. In this app the repeat is written out, so the piece is 78 bars long.

analysis.title: A over E
analysis.text: A major with E in the bass: A, C sharp and E. The melody climbs C sharp, D, E in this bar and again in the next.

analysis.title: Busy bar
analysis.text: Bar 37 is the busiest of the piece. The bass walks E2, B2, E3 while two chords sound above it, D with A and then G with D and B, under a held F sharp 4. No single hand can play all of it, so this app gives the right hand the two chords and keeps the bass in the left hand.
analysis.function: submediant seventh over an E bass

analysis.title: A minor 7
analysis.text: Each hand plays one long chord for the whole bar. A minor seventh: the left hand plays A2 and G3, the right hand C, E, A and C. The chord is minor, with a natural C, so there is no C sharp to pull the music toward D.

analysis.title: D major
analysis.text: The first ending closes on a plain D major chord: D, F sharp and A with D again on top in the right hand, D, A and D in the left. Then the music goes back to bar 1 (bar 40 of this app).

analysis.title: Repeat
analysis.text: Bars 40 to 70 are bars 1 to 31 again, written out: the same notes, the same chords and the same fingers.

analysis.title: Second ending
analysis.text: The second ending starts like the first, on E minor, then turns to the notes G, F, B, C, E and D with no sharp anywhere: every note of bars 71 to 78 is a white key. The chords all fit D Dorian, the mode with F and C natural.

analysis.title: D minor over E
analysis.text: D, F and A with E in the bass: a D minor chord over an E bass. The F is natural, the same note that darkened bar 21.
analysis.function: tonic minor over an E bass

analysis.title: F major 7
analysis.text: F, A and C over an E bass: F major seventh, the E being its major seventh. The melody climbs B, C, F.

analysis.title: B half dim.
analysis.text: The bass line and the chords of bar 37 come back, but the held melody note is F natural instead of F sharp. With F, the notes B, D, F and A make a B half diminished chord over the E bass.
analysis.function: half diminished over an E bass

analysis.title: D minor
analysis.text: The piece ends on D minor: D, F and A (F natural) with D on top in the right hand, D, A and D in the left. The first ending closed on D major; the last chord of the piece is its minor version.

beginner.summary: Gymnopédie No. 1 by Erik Satie, with the repeat and both endings written out: 78 bars in 3/4, felt as three slow beats. The right hand sings the melody and the left hand keeps one pattern: a low bass note on beat 1, then a chord on beats 2 and 3. Many players know this sound from calm video-game piano music such as Minecraft's, which is often compared to Satie's style. It is a simplified version of the transcribed bars, so read the Arrangement note to see what was left out.

handPositions.text: Bar 1: the little finger (5) on the low G for one beat, then the chord B3, D4 and F#4 with fingers 5, 3 and 1, held for two beats. Bar 2 is the same shape from D2 with the chord A3, C#4 and F#4. The right hand rests for four bars.
Bar 5, beat 2: the melody enters. F#5 with finger 3, then A5 with the little finger (5). The left hand keeps its pattern of one bass note and one chord.
Bar 6: G5 (4), F#5 (3) and C#5 (1). The thumb takes the C#5 so that it can step down to B4 in the next bar.
Bar 7: B4 (1), C#5 (2) and D5 (3), three steps up with three neighbouring fingers.
Bar 8: A4 with finger 2, held for the whole bar. The thumb (1) will take the F#4 in bar 9.
Bars 9 to 12: F#4 with the thumb (1), held for four bars (the note is tied from bar to bar). Count the bars while the left hand keeps going.
Bars 13 to 16 repeat bars 5 to 8 with the same fingers. The one difference is the A4 of bar 16: it takes the thumb (1) because C#5 comes next.
Bars 17 and 18: C#5 (3), then F#5 (5), one note per bar.
Bar 17: the bass moves to F#2 for the first time, with the chord A3, C#4 and F#4. Bar 18 is B1 with B3, D4 and F#4.
Bars 19 to 21: E4 with finger 2, held for three bars (tied). The left hand plays E minor, E minor 7 and then D minor.
Bar 21: D minor. The bass is D2 and the chord is F3, A3 and D4: the F is natural here.
Bar 22: A4 (1), B4 (2) and C5 (3). The C is natural. Bar 23 is E5 (5), D5 (4) and B4 (2); bar 24 is D5 (4), C5 (3) and B4 (2).
From bar 23 the bass stays on D2 for nine bars (bars 23 to 31). Only the chord above it changes, so the left hand can relax into a pattern.
Bar 25: D5 (4), tied into bar 26. The last D5 of bar 26 takes the thumb (1) to start the climb of bar 27.
Bar 29: E5 (3), D5 (2) and B4 (1). Bars 30 and 31: D5 (3) held, and a last D5 (2) on beat 3 to lead into the ending.
Bar 32 begins the first ending: G5 with the little finger (5), then F#5 (4) in bar 33. In bar 34 play B4 (2), A4 (1) and B4 (2); bars 35 and 36 are C#5 (3), D5 (4) and E5 (5) twice.
Bar 37: F#4 with finger 3, held for the bar. The left hand plays E2 on beat 1, then the chords D4 with A3 and G4 with D4 and B3. The little bass steps of the Original (B2 and E3) are left out.
Bar 38: the right hand plays three notes at once, E4, A4 and C5 (fingers 1, 3 and 5), and the left hand A2 with G3. Bar 39 is F#4, A4 and D5 over D2, A2 and D3: a D major chord.
Bar 40: back to the start. The repeat is written out, so bars 40 to 70 are bars 1 to 31 again with the same fingers.
Bar 71 begins the second ending: G5 (5), then F5 (4) in bar 72. In bar 73 play B4 (1), C5 (2) and F5 (5); in bars 74 and 75 play E5 (4), D5 (3) and C5 (2).
Bar 76: F4 with finger 3, the natural F instead of the F sharp of bar 37. The left hand plays E2 and the same two chords as in bar 37.
Bar 78, the last bar: F4, A4 and D5 in the right hand over D2, A2 and D3 in the left. This is a D minor chord, so the F is natural. Hold it and let it fade.

beginner.posture: Sit centered with your forearms level and your shoulders loose. The left hand leaps from a low note to a chord in every bar, so move from the elbow and keep the wrist soft. Play every note quietly and slowly: this piece has no loud moments.
practicePlan: Start with the left hand alone (press Mute right): bar 1 is a low G then a chord, bar 2 a low D then a chord. Play them for four bars until the leap feels easy.
Then the right hand alone (press Mute left), starting at bar 5, beat 2. Use Loop a section on Melody enters, with Slow on.
Put the hands together on Melody enters, then on Held F sharp: the right hand holds one note for four bars while the left hand keeps leaping.
Learn the next sections one at a time (F sharp minor to D minor, then Rising line, then First ending), each with Loop a section.
Switch on Metronome at 60 beats per minute and count three slow beats a bar. The repeat plays the same bars again, so only the Second ending (bars 71 to 78) is new at the end.
beginner.arrangementNote: Simplified from the transcribed Original level (Mutopia-2014/12/14-37). The right hand plays the melody and tied notes stay tied; in the last two bars of each ending it plays the three upper notes of the chord. The left hand plays the bass for one beat and the chord for two beats (the printed bass lasts a whole bar and is held with the pedal); a chord of four notes keeps its three upper notes; in bars 37 and 76 the left hand plays E2 and the two chords, and the small bass notes B2 and E3 are left out. The fingering is editorial: the source prints none.

interpretation.rubato: Keep the beat steady while you learn the notes. The source marks Lent et douloureux (slow and sorrowful) and nothing else about time, so once the notes are secure let the melody breathe a little at the ends of the phrases, never rushing.
interpretation.dynamics: Play softly throughout and keep the chord quieter than the bass note. The melody enters at pp in bar 5.

original.summary: The Original level is Satie's Gymnopédie No. 1 as printed in the Mutopia source, with the repeat and both endings written out (78 bars in 3/4). The left hand holds a low bass note for the whole bar and plays a chord on beats 2 and 3; the right hand sings the melody, which enters in bar 5 after four bars of the left hand alone. Many players know this sound from calm video-game piano music such as Minecraft's, which is often compared to Satie's style. Switch on Analysis to see the chords and the notes behind them.

handPositions.text: Bars 1 to 4: the left hand alone. A low G (G2) with the little finger (5) held for the whole bar, and on beat 2 the chord B3, D4 and F#4 with fingers 5, 3 and 1. Bar 2 is D2 with A3, C#4 and F#4.
Bar 5, beat 2: the melody enters, pp. F#5 with finger 3 and A5 with the little finger (5). The source prints no fingering, so these fingers are editorial.
Bars 9 to 12: F#4 with the thumb (1), held and tied for four bars.
Bars 13 to 16 repeat bars 5 to 8, with the same fingers.
Bar 17: the bass moves to F#2 with the chord A3, C#4 and F#4. Bar 18 is B1 with B3, D4 and F#4.
Bars 19 to 21: E4 with finger 2 tied for three bars, while the left hand plays chords from the bass staff: B3 with G3 (bar 19), then G4, D4 and B3 (bar 20), then D4, A3 and F3 (bar 21).
Bar 22: A4 (1), B4 (2) and C5 (3), then E5 (5), D5 (4) and B4 (2) in bar 23.
From bar 23 to bar 31 the bass stays on D2 and the chords change above it. Bars 24 to 26 and 29 to 31 have four-note chords, played with fingers 5, 3, 2 and 1.
Bar 27: E5 (2), F5 (3) and G5 (4); bar 28: A5 (5), C5 (1) and D5 (2). The thumb on the D5 of bar 26 prepares this climb.
Bar 32 begins the first ending: G5 (5), F#5 (4), then B4 (2), A4 (1) and B4 (2) in bar 34.

Bar 37: the left hand holds E2 (finger 5) as the lower voice and plays B2 (finger 2) and E3 (finger 1) in the upper voice. The right hand plays the two chords: A3 with D4 (fingers 1 and 3) and B3, D4, G4 (fingers 1, 2 and 5).
Bar 38: a four-note right-hand chord C4, E4, A4 and C5 (fingers 1, 2, 4 and 5) over A2 and G3. Bar 39 is D4, F#4, A4 and D5 over D2, A2 and D3.
Bar 40: the repeat, written out. Bars 40 to 70 repeat bars 1 to 31 with the same notes and fingers.
Bar 71 begins the second ending: G5 (5), F5 (4), then B4 (1), C5 (2) and F5 (5) in bar 73, and E5, D5, C5 (4, 3, 2) in bars 74 and 75.
Bar 78, the last bar: D4, F4, A4 and D5 (fingers 1, 2, 4 and 5) over D2, A2 and D3. A D minor chord that ends the piece.

original.posture: Sit as in the Beginner lesson. The bass note is held for the whole bar while the same hand plays the chord, so the pedal does the holding. The source prints no pedal; a natural choice, editorial and not printed, is down with each bass note and up as the next one arrives. The chords of bars 24 to 26 and 29 to 31 have four notes, so keep the hand open.
practicePlan: Read the left hand alone first: a bass note, then a chord an octave or more higher. Practise the leap bar by bar without the pedal.
Add the pedal as an editorial choice: down with each bass note, up as the next one arrives. The source prints none.
Learn the right hand by sections (Melody enters, Held F sharp, Melody again, F sharp minor to D minor, Rising line) with Loop a section and Slow.
Bars 37 and 76 are the hardest: the left hand holds E2 and plays B2 and E3 above it while the right hand plays two chords. Loop them on their own.
Join the sections, switch on Analysis, and raise the tempo with Ramp toward 60 beats per minute.
original.arrangementNote: Transcribed from the Mutopia Project LilyPond source (Mutopia-2014/12/14-37, typeset by Evin Robertson from the Dover edition, Public Domain) and checked note by note against the MIDI file that LilyPond makes from it: the whole piece, 78 bars: the body of bars 1 to 31, the first ending (bars 32 to 39), the repeat written out (bars 40 to 70) and the second ending (bars 71 to 78). The source prints no fingering and no pedal, so every finger here is editorial. The source writes the left-hand chords on the treble staff in bars 1 to 18 and in the endings, and on the bass staff in bars 19 to 31; the app gives them all to the left hand, an editorial choice, and draws the left hand on the bass staff with ledger lines. In bars 37 and 76 the right hand takes the two chords, also editorial, because three streams of notes cannot be played by one hand.

interpretation.rubato: The source marks Lent et douloureux (slow and sorrowful) and prints no other tempo or time mark. Keep the beat even and very slow; the 60 beats per minute of this app is the speed of the Mutopia MIDI file, not a printed tempo.
interpretation.dynamics: The source file marks pp at bar 5 and again at bar 13, p at bar 22 and an f under the chord of bar 9, which the MIDI file cannot confirm; hairpins swell and fade over the phrases. Keep the left-hand chords lighter than the bass note and the melody above both.

sources.what: Mutopia Project piece 37 (Mutopia-2014/12/14-37), Gymnopédie No. 1 for piano by Erik Satie (1888), typeset in LilyPond 2.18.2 by Evin Robertson from the Dover edition (a reproduction of the original publication; the Dover translations are not in the file). Public Domain: the typesetter placed the file in the public domain, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/publicdomain . Transcribed from the LilyPond file: the whole piece, 78 bars: the body of bars 1 to 31, the first ending (bars 32 to 39), the repeat written out (bars 40 to 70) and the second ending (bars 71 to 78). The notes were read from the file with a throwaway program that resolves its relative octaves, durations and ties and unfolds the repeat (it is not part of this repository), and every onset of the result was checked against the MIDI file listed next. The source prints no fingering, no pedal and no tempo number.

MIDI file that LilyPond generated from the same source. It plays the music as written, the body of bars 1 to 31 once and then the two endings one after the other (47 bars), with no repeat. It was used to check every octave and onset (282 note onsets, pinned in tests/fixtures); the repeat of bars 1 to 31 is the same notes again.

confidence.note: Pitches and rhythms come from one typeset source (Mutopia, from the Dover edition) and match its own MIDI file note for note, onset by onset. There is no independent second edition, because no printed scan was read.

The source prints no fingering. Every finger in both levels is editorial: the right hand follows the hand position of each phrase, and the left hand uses 5 on the bass and 5, 3, 1 (or 5, 3, 2, 1) on the chord.

The hands are editorial. The source writes the left-hand chords on the treble staff for bars 1 to 18 and the endings, and on the bass staff for bars 19 to 31. The app gives all of them to the left hand, except the two chords of bars 37 and 76, which it gives to the right hand because the left hand already has three bass notes there.
The source has the marking Lent et douloureux and no tempo number. The 60 beats per minute (quarter note) is the default speed of the Mutopia MIDI file, not an edition's tempo.

The source writes a repeat with two endings. The data writes it out, so it is 78 bars: bars 1 to 31, the first ending, bars 1 to 31 again, the second ending. The MIDI file plays the two endings in a row and no repeat, so the repeat is checked by the test that bars 40 to 70 repeat bars 1 to 31.

The key signature has two sharps, which fits D major and B minor, and the source declares B minor. The data says D major because the first ending closes on a D major chord and the chords alternate between G and D major sevenths. The second ending closes on D minor, so the tonic is D in both; the major or minor third is what changes.

Editorial simplification of the transcribed bars: the left hand holds the bass for one beat and the chord for two, a chord of four notes keeps its three upper notes, the right hand keeps the melody (three notes of each final chord), and in bars 37 and 76 the small bass notes B2 and E3 are left out. It is not a printed edition.

The roman numerals and the notes about the harmony are read from the transcribed notes and checked by tests against the data; no published analysis was consulted. Reading the piece in D major, and bars 21 to 31 as a D pedal with colors above it, is a judgment of this app.

Dynamics are not stored in the data. They are read from the source file: pp at bars 5 and 13, p at bar 22, hairpins over the phrases, and an f under the chord of bar 9 that looks odd in so quiet a piece and could not be checked against a scan.
